Feature-wise drift tests between two windows

Source: R/dfr_dde.R
dde_feature_drift.Rd

Tests every feature for drift between a reference window and an analysis window, with the univariate tests used by Szucs and Nemeth (2025).

Usage

dde_feature_drift(reference, current, test = "js", threshold = NULL)

Arguments

reference

Data frame or matrix with the reference window.

current

Data frame or matrix with the analysis window, with the same columns.

test

One of "js", "ks" or "wasserstein".

threshold

Drift threshold. NULL uses the default of the test.

Value

data frame with one row per feature and the columns feature, statistic (the distance, or the p-value for "ks") and drift.

Details

The tests follow the definitions and defaults of the Evidently library:

  • "js": Jensen-Shannon distance (natural logarithm) between the histograms of the two windows, on common bins chosen with Sturges' rule over both windows; empty bins get a proportion of 1e-4. Drift when the distance is at least threshold (default 0.1).

  • "ks": two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Drift when the p-value is below threshold (default 0.05).

  • "wasserstein": Wasserstein distance divided by the standard deviation of the reference window (at least 0.001). Drift when it is at least threshold (default 0.1).

Missing values are dropped; features with fewer than two values in either window are not tested.

The distances of the "js" test do not shrink to 0 between two samples of the same distribution: with a few hundred observations per window the Jensen-Shannon distance of identical distributions is often close to the default threshold. Use windows of about a thousand observations, or a higher threshold, with small windows.

Examples

set.seed(1)
reference <- data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(300), y = stats::rnorm(300))
current <- data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(300, mean = 1), y = stats::rnorm(300))
dde_feature_drift(reference, current, test = "ks")
#>   feature    statistic drift
#> 1       x 2.914443e-18  TRUE
#> 2       y 7.870443e-01 FALSE
